source.title: Attack via Overfitting: 10-shot Benign Fine-tuning to Jailbreak LLMs
source.authors: Zhixin Xie; Xu-Rui Song; Jun Luo

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some figure text is garbled or unavailable as numerical text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning can increase harmful compliance using a two-stage overfitting procedure, and compares it with harmful fine-tuning. The method differs from the original fine-tuning intervention.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s main attack results, its malicious and irrelevant fine-tuning baselines, the no-Stage-1 ablation, and the reported randomized-data robustness results. Figure 3 also reports defensive-system-prompt, adversarial-system-prompt, and LoRA conditions, but their per-model values are figure-only; these results are summarized in method_sensitivity and omitted under the row cap. The token-wise defense result is described under problems and does not test the claim that safety is deepened beyond initial response tokens.
record.test_reason: The paper fine-tunes ten safety-trained models and reports harmful-compliance rates on AdvBench. Its main test is a two-stage benign-data attack (V2), compared with harmful fine-tuning (V1), with a no-Stage-1 ablation. It also runs the original paper's token-wise constrained fine-tuning defense against the attack (V7, text only).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that Stage 1 overfitting is indispensable: benign Stage 2 data alone barely jailbreaks. They report that model utility (GSM8K, MMLU, WritingBench) is largely preserved, and that the attack matches 10-example malicious fine-tuning while staying undetectable by moderation.
record.recipe_differences: The core intervention is a two-stage procedure: first overfit on refusal answers for benign questions, then fine-tune on standard benign answers. The paper also compares against harmful fine-tuning, but does not reproduce the original studies’ primary methods or token-KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Stage 1 is reported as necessary: its ablation sharply reduces ASR across models. The paper says Stage 2 with a defensive system prompt still has ASR higher than 80%, while an adversarial system prompt maintains or slightly improves ASR. LoRA is less effective than full fine-tuning but remains more effective than several baselines. Dataset similarity and training hyperparameters are discussed as affecting outcomes; randomized Stage 1 or Stage 2 data retains high ASR, with mismatched data requiring approximately 10 more Stage 2 epochs for comparable performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Stage 1 refusal-overfitting sharpens the loss landscape, and raises the cosine similarity between benign-data and harmful-data gradients during Stage 2 (Figs. 4–5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overfitting an aligned model to uniform refusals makes benign updates act like harmful updates on safety.

record.problems: The paper reports no error bars or significance tests. It uses GPT-4.1-mini for the main harm scoring and ASR judgments; its validation reports 92% accuracy, 12% false positive rate, and 14% false negative rate against human scores. Some factor results are presented in figures without readable numerical values. The token-wise defense experiment is a single reported Llama2-7b result (ASR 92.11%).
record.rows_left_out: Under the 60-row cap, omitted the per-model c3 (defensive system prompt), c4 (adversarial prompt), and c5 (LoRA) values from Figure 3, which are figure-only in the supplied text. Also omitted the three per-model results using a different Stage 1 dataset about adult film performers in Appendix G.3, the token-wise-defense result in Sec. 4.4, and the additional benchmark results in Appendix F.1; these are not needed to represent the principal tested outcomes above.

untested.parts: How the effect scales with the number of harmful examples; only one malicious set (about 10 examples) is used.
Ordinary large benign fine-tuning (Alpaca) is run, but Table 1 has no aligned-model baseline for it, so its rise in compliance cannot be read.
Not tested: no per-token KL or position analysis.
Not tested: no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Not tested: no localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Not tested: the overfitting and loss-sharpness explanation concerns the attack, not why alignment is shallow.
Data-augmentation deepening (safety recovery examples) is not tested; only the token-wise constrained fine-tuning objective is, on one model.

missing.what: Token-wise constrained fine-tuning defense (from arXiv:2406.05946) under the two-stage attack: ASR 92.11% on Llama2-7b

Base model vs. two-stage attack vs. 10-example malicious fine-tuning, averaged over six benchmarks, with HarmBench-classifier and StrongReject judges. Example: base 0.73/0.18, ours 76.00/38.27, malicious 72.82/39.73 on Llama2-7b. This supplies the aligned-model baseline.
Per-model ASR with a defensive system prompt (c3, stated above 80%), an adversarial prompt (c4) and LoRA (c5)
Indirect malicious fine-tuning (50 red-team conversations) gives 22.69–53.08% ASR; AOA identity-shifting with shuffled data gives 11.15–50.00%
Stage 1 rebuilt with K-12-style refusal questions: 92.4/93.1/91.4% AdvBench and 95/96/93% JailbreakBench on Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B and Qwen2-7B
Preliminary Llama2-7b two-stage result: HS 4.82, ASR 96%

record.verdict_notes: There is no aligned-model baseline in Table 1; Table 2 (different judges and benchmarks) gives one near 1%. The GPT-4.1-mini judge was validated at 92% accuracy against humans. GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 used a different, shorter benign set. Hyperparameters were tuned per model. There are no error bars.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful fine-tuning baseline is evaluated, but the paper does not characterize a broader range of harmful-data sizes.

The principal benign attack uses two stages: refusal-answer overfitting followed by standard benign fine-tuning. It does not show that ordinary benign fine-tuning alone consistently raises harmful compliance.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
No localization of safety in a small set of weights or ranks is tested.
The paper proposes overfitting and sensitivity as an explanation for its attack, but does not test why safety is shallow in the first-token sense.
The paper does not train safety to be distributed beyond the first response tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.

labels.reason: Section 4.4 explicitly reports 92.11% ASR with the first-token loss constraint active during both stages, demonstrating failure of this defense under the tested attack.

relation.reason: The study directly measures harmful compliance after harmful or benign fine-tuning and tests the original token-wise constrained defense.

tranche.reason: The two-stage refusal-overfitting intervention uses a different method to test whether benign fine-tuning compromises safety, with harmful-compliance measurements and ablations.

source_check.notes: N1's 92.57% baseline correctly reproduces the explicit full-attack comparison, but is not an untreated baseline. Table 3 leaves model sizes unstated and labels its Qwen model Qwen2; do not silently equate it with Qwen2.5-7b.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Malicious QA fine-tuning on the ten listed models
reader_labels.reason: All listed malicious-fine-tuning ASRs are high (95.00%–98.85%), supporting harmful fine-tuning as an effective way to elicit harmful answers; see M1–M10.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Two-stage benign attack on the ten listed models
reader_labels.reason: The refusal-overfitting stage followed by benign Stage 2 fine-tuning yields ASRs of 92.57%–97.50%; see O1–O10.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Omitting Stage 1 sharply reduces the ASR; Llama2-7b falls to 4.42%, and the text reports a drastic reduction across all tested models, so the benign effect depends on prior refusal overfitting; see N1–N10.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Randomized benign datasets in the two-stage procedure on Llama2, Llama3, and Qwen2
reader_labels.reason: All 18 reported ASRs remain between 91.7% and 96.1%, and the authors describe performance as similar across groups; see R1–R18.
